chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Rashid, from Sama'ah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is certain of the Replacement (by Allah), his soul will be generous with expenditure.'

key_terms.الْخَلَف: The Replacement (divine promise to replace what is spent)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of spending in the way of God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith links the concept of 'al-khalaf' (divine replacement) to the psychological state of 'sakha' (contentment/generosity), suggesting that certainty in Allah's promise to replace spent wealth removes the sting of expenditure. This reflects the Shia emphasis on tawakkul (trust in God) as a spiritual mechanism that transforms financial anxiety into active charity, reinforcing the ethical imperative of spending in the path of Allah.
